physicalNotes: No radius or mass of the Great Attractor is recorded: it is an extended region toward which galaxies stream, and its package frames it at 15000000 pc (object.json worldFrame.bodyRadiusM), a presentation value: chosen to show the galaxies around the fitted point; Lynden-Bell et al. (1988) publish no radius.

sources.position: Galactic longitude 307, latitude 9: the centre of the flow Lynden-Bell et al. (1988) fitted to the motions of 400 elliptical galaxies (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1988ApJ...326...19L), turned to ICRS with the IAU 1958 galactic frame.
sources.distance: 64070000 pc: the Planck 2018 comoving distance (https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.06209) of the fitted 4350 +/- 350 km/s (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1988ApJ...326...19L), the conversion the Nearby Universe field uses for its redshift galaxies, so the point sits among the galaxies drawn around it.
sources.properMotion: Zero: the region toward which galaxies stream is held at its published position; no motion across the sky is applied.
sources.radialVelocity: 4350 +/- 350 km/s in the Hubble flow, the fitted distance of the attractor: Lynden-Bell et al. (1988), Galaxy streaming toward the new supergalactic center, ApJ 326, 19 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1988ApJ...326...19L)
